sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Arbaugh v. Y & H Corp. asks if the 15-employee rule limits federal court jurisdiction. The lower court treated this number as a jurisdictional bar. The parties disagree on whether this threshold defines court power or a claim element.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Arbaugh wants the Court to treat the 15-employee rule as a jurisdictional limit.
Y & H Corp. wants the Court to treat the 15-employee rule as a claim element.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Arbaugh argues the statute grants jurisdiction only to employers with 15 or more employees.
Y & H Corp. argues the employee count is a factual element of the discrimination claim.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines whether federal courts can dismiss discrimination claims based solely on employee count. It defines the scope of federal judicial power over Title VII disputes. It clarifies the procedural path for plaintiffs with smaller employers.
